record.question:
A web application runs on EC2 instances in private subnets across two Availability Zones behind an internet-facing ALB. Each private subnet routes outbound internet traffic through a NAT instance in its own AZ. Login works, but a server-side request to a map provider fails for about half of page loads.

Requests fail only from one AZ. Its NAT instance is stopped; the application instances are healthy, and route-table and network ACL configurations are otherwise correct. The company wants to restore access and reduce NAT maintenance.

Which solution best addresses the failure?

options.text: Add outbound network ACL rules for the map provider’s addresses and restrict future network ACL changes with IAM policies.
Enable ALB cross-zone load balancing so every server-side request to the map provider uses the healthy AZ’s NAT instance.
Increase the stopped NAT instance’s instance size and retain one manually managed NAT instance per AZ.
Replace the NAT instances with a public zonal NAT gateway in each AZ. Route each private subnet to its same-AZ gateway, and route the gateways’ public subnets to an internet gateway.

explanation.text:
<<4>> repairs the confirmed outbound failure and replaces self-managed instances with AWS-managed NAT gateways. A zonal gateway in each AZ avoids making one AZ’s egress depend on another AZ.

<<1>> changes a control already verified as correct. <<2>> confuses inbound ALB distribution with outbound routing: an application instance uses its subnet route table for the map call. <<3>> does not establish a capacity problem and retains the maintenance and failover burden.

A 50% failure rate alone would not prove a NAT outage; the stopped instance and AZ-specific tests supply the decisive evidence. NAT gateways need correct routing and do not make external providers highly available.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-comparison.html

diagram_alt: Both applications pass inbound health checks, while the stopped NAT path isolates outbound failure to one AZ.

sources.supports: NAT gateway management, per-AZ redundancy, zone-independent deployment, and migration routing.

editorial_notes: Added discriminating operational evidence rather than treating 50% failures as proof. Specified a zonal NAT gateway per AZ and removed cross-AZ ambiguity. Answer ID unchanged.
